Record a change to a rating's lifecycle

Source: R/lifecycle.R
set_lifecycle.Rd

A rating starts as a "draft". This is how a person moves it on, and it is the only way: nothing in the package changes a lifecycle by itself, and nothing sets "approved" except this function called by a named person. Each change records who made it, when and why, in the rating's provenance and as a step in rating_history(). The earlier version is kept, so the rating can be checked against what it was.

The states and where each may go next:

FromMay go to
draftunder_review, withdrawn
under_reviewapproved, draft (returned for rework), withdrawn
approvedunder_review (re-review), superseded, withdrawn
superseded, withdrawnnowhere: make a new rating

Approval has its own conditions. It must come from under_review, so no rating is approved without having been put up for review. It is refused for a rating that fails its own validity checks (rating_invariants()). The person who put a rating under review may approve it too, which is the default, but that is written into the reason so that a reader of the record can see it. Set allow_self_approval = FALSE to require a second person.

Amending a rating (setting its operational limits, aligning its limbs) makes a new draft, because what was reviewed is no longer what exists. That shows in rating_history(); the records here stay.

Usage

set_lifecycle(x, to, by, reason, at = Sys.time(), allow_self_approval = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A FlodeRating or FlodeSegmentedRating. A FlodeRatingTable has nowhere to keep who, when and why, and is refused.

to

The lifecycle to move to: one of "draft", "under_review", "approved", "superseded", "withdrawn".

by

Character. Who is making the change. A name, not a role.

reason

Character. Why. Required for every change.

at

The time of the change. Default now.

allow_self_approval

Logical. If TRUE (default), the person who put a rating under review may also approve it, and the record says so. If FALSE, a second person must approve. Names are compared ignoring case and surrounding spaces.

Value

A new rating with its lifecycle changed. The original is not altered.

See also

rating_lifecycle() for the record, rating_history(), rating_invariants().

Examples

set.seed(1)
stage <- seq(0.3, 3, length.out = 25)
gaugings <- data.frame(stage_m = stage,
                       discharge_cms = 3 * stage^1.6 * exp(rnorm(25, sd = 0.03)))
fit <- fit_rating(gaugings, quiet = TRUE)

reviewed <- set_lifecycle(fit, "under_review", by = "A. Analyst",
                          reason = "Fitted from the 2024 gaugings; ready for review")
approved <- set_lifecycle(reviewed, "approved", by = "B. Reviewer",
                          reason = "Checked the assessment and the sensitivity tests")
rating_lifecycle(approved)[, c("from", "to", "by")]
#>            from           to          by
#>          <char>       <char>      <char>
#> 1:        draft under_review  A. Analyst
#> 2: under_review     approved B. Reviewer
rating_history(approved)[, c("step", "lifecycle", "note")]
#>     step    lifecycle
#>    <int>       <char>
#> 1:     1        draft
#> 2:     2 under_review
#> 3:     3     approved
#>                                                                                                                   note
#>                                                                                                                 <char>
#> 1:                                                                                                                <NA>
#> 2:      lifecycle: draft to under_review by A. Analyst on 2026-11-27 (Fitted from the 2024 gaugings; ready for review)
#> 3: lifecycle: under_review to approved by B. Reviewer on 2026-11-27 (Checked the assessment and the sensitivity tests)
